cards.title: Conservativity of internal parametricity for function-free judgments
cards.formal: Does adding the source’s internal-parametricity structure preserve all inhabitation judgments whose context and result type use no function types? The proposed form is: for every context Γ and type A in a common function-free fragment of the base and parametric theories, if Γ⊢M:A is derivable in the parametric extension for some term M, then Γ⊢N:A is derivable in the base theory for some term N. The restriction is on Γ and A, not on the intermediate types or constructions in the extended derivation. The source calls the destination ordinary type theory but does not fully specify that calculus or the common fragment, so this is a recovered conjecture schema rather than a complete formal benchmark.
cards.why: Would clarify which conclusions proved using internal relational principles can be transferred back to an ordinary type theory, and thus how much proof strength the added parametricity contributes on a restricted language.
cards.status_note: Read the exact conference conjecture, checked the expanded LMCS formalisms and discussion, and the later authors’ implementation abstract. Conservativity searches through 12 September 2026 found no matching resolution. The source’s target calculus and fragment remain insufficiently specified.

progress.text: The conference conclusion proposes conservativity for contexts and result types without function types, after identifying failure for unrestricted statements.
The expanded paper supplies richer formal presentations and semantics but does not provide the matching syntactic theorem in the checked discussion.
An implementation and mechanized internal-parametricity results are reported for Cubical Agda; these do not settle the reverse conservativity assertion.

sentences: The conjecture concerns proofs made in a type theory with internal parametricity.
It asks whether an inhabited type already has an inhabitant in the base theory when the assumptions and result type contain no function types.
The richer derivation itself may use function types and parametricity.
Unrestricted conservativity is already ruled out by the source, but the restricted claim lacks an exact base calculus and fragment grammar.
Later semantic and implementation developments are distinguished from the missing syntactic conservativity theorem.

cards.definitions: A context Γ is an ordered list x₁:A₁,…,x_j:A_j of typed variables, where A_i may depend on earlier variables. A judgment Γ⊢M:A asserts that M is a term of type A under those assumptions. Inhabitation means the existence of such a term. A dependent function type Π(x:B).C classifies functions taking x:B to a result in C, which may depend on x; B→C is the nondependent case. The source excludes function types from the statement and assumptions of the proposed conservative fragment. It does not give an inductive grammar deciding all permitted type expressions, including expressions represented inside universes. Internal parametricity adds types and terms expressing relational behavior inside the theory itself. In the paper, paths represent equality-like structure and bridges represent relations; the extension includes bridge and Gel constructions in addition to cartesian cubical structure. A common fragment must contain expressions meaningful in the target calculus, not just extended types that happen to lack an arrow symbol. Conservativity for the stated fragment would preserve existence of inhabitants; it does not demand that the extended term M itself be a term of the smaller language, or that M and N be judgmentally equal. A syntactic proof transformation would compute a base derivation from an extended derivation. Semantic validity in one model, consistency and canonicity for a particular closed type are different claims and do not by themselves state this general derivability property. Which of the cubical, universe, path and inductive rules are retained in the base remains part of the missing specification.
cards.answer_criterion: For fully specified source and target calculi and the intended common fragment, prove that every extended derivation of an inhabitation judgment in the fragment has a base derivation, or exhibit a judgment in that same fragment which is derivable only in the extension. If an effective translation is part of the intended target, its input, output and derivation-preservation requirement must also be fixed. The current source does not determine all these choices. A model construction alone or a result for a chosen smaller class of judgments does not certify the whole schema.

context_blocks.title: Why the function-free restriction appears
context_blocks.text: The conference paper explicitly warns that unrestricted conservativity fails. It gives a statement asserting that every map from a universe to the booleans takes the same value at the unit and empty types: this is provable using parametricity but fails in classical cubical sets. The proposed function-free restriction follows that example.

context_blocks.title: The proof may use the richer theory
context_blocks.text: The intended benefit is to reason with internal parametricity while obtaining a conclusion available in the original language. Restricting every step of the proof to the base language would remove that distinction and would not express the conjecture in the concluding paragraph.

context_blocks.title: Later formalisms do not identify this target for us
context_blocks.text: The 2021 expanded paper develops formal and computational presentations and a model of internal parametricity. The checked sections do not supply a syntactic conservativity theorem matching the conference question’s unspecified ordinary target and function-free fragment.

context_blocks.title: Implementation progress is a different guarantee
context_blocks.text: The 2024 authors’ abstract describes Agda --bridges, mechanized internal-parametricity theorems and compatibility with the existing cubical library. Supporting base proofs in an extension does not establish the reverse statement that every new proof of a common judgment has a base proof.

cards.context:
The conference paper explicitly warns that unrestricted conservativity fails. It gives a statement asserting that every map from a universe to the booleans takes the same value at the unit and empty types: this is provable using parametricity but fails in classical cubical sets. The proposed function-free restriction follows that example.

The intended benefit is to reason with internal parametricity while obtaining a conclusion available in the original language. Restricting every step of the proof to the base language would remove that distinction and would not express the conjecture in the concluding paragraph.

The 2021 expanded paper develops formal and computational presentations and a model of internal parametricity. The checked sections do not supply a syntactic conservativity theorem matching the conference question’s unspecified ordinary target and function-free fragment.

The 2024 authors’ abstract describes Agda --bridges, mechanized internal-parametricity theorems and compatibility with the existing cubical library. Supporting base proofs in an extension does not establish the reverse statement that every new proof of a common judgment has a base proof.

meta.status_scope: No claim of exhaustive open-status verification
methodology: Detailed cards have individually written statements, context, significance, and documented results. Source notes are unfinished research records and do not yet meet that standard. The legacy index is retained for traceability.
Open in the source means open at the date of that source. The build date, 10 September 2026, does not establish current open status. Old excerpts may omit conditions or subsequent results.

Selection considers model power, necessary resources, sharp bounds, structural characterizations, explicit constructions, and minimal assumptions. Source notes use a heuristic screen; detailed cards give an individual explanation.

The earlier automatic paper screen allowed at most one new card per paper title and rejected identical formulations and close duplicates within a source. Approved textbook and survey imports retain multiple distinct questions per publication. Confirmed overlaps supplement existing cards; collection-wide semantic deduplication remains incomplete.

Short quotations retain the source language. Later related literature, where listed, is a research aid rather than evidence of resolution. Personal notes and saved cards are stored locally in your browser.

Textbook and survey questions are dated paraphrases; source locations, conjectures, research directions and caveats are preserved on the problem cards. These annotations do not establish current open status or change a later card review. New source drafts remain unassessed for importance. The reader contains the imported questions and external bibliographic references only; source files are not bundled.

Selection groups follow the agreed 10 large and 25 small categories. We aim for benchmarks of 100 and 500 problems, with a possible expansion to 1,000. All three use the same category order and the same ranking within each category. The respective prefixes are 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 problems per large/small category. The possible 1,000-problem expansion has 1000 assigned places and 0 reserved places. Each card records its category explicitly. These counts describe saved candidates; classification does not verify a statement or its current open status. Deleted records are absent from the catalogue and exports. Their stable IDs and reasons are retained to prevent reimport. Final quota selection and a comprehensive deduplication audit remain pending.

Importance ordering is an editorial assessment of foundational significance, breadth of consequences, and influence on other questions. Each assessed card gives a reason. The category-wide review also uses shared priority bands for questions of comparable scope; it does not claim that these ties have a scientifically meaningful internal order. Unassessed drafts share a provisional score of 50; their relative order is only an ID tie-break, not an importance judgment. The first 5/2 places in each large/small category are an explicit editorial focus selection balancing importance and topical diversity. Focus ordering does not alter importance scores; remaining candidates use score and ID order. The targets are 100 and 500 problems, with a possible expansion to 1,000. Top 100, Top 500 and the possible Top 1000 use the first 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 category places respectively, all from the same ranking. Category positions include all candidates and remain fixed when filtering. Publication date, source date, and card detail do not increase importance. Records marked resolved are placed after the remaining candidates, without changing their historical importance score. Importance review does not establish that a saved question is still open.
